_: THE QUESTIONS THE DOOR ASKS ITSELF (Create Indicator, clarify first). Owner direction, 2026-11-18: when a choice that changes the maths is not settled, ask ONE short question with the options before building; never guess. Each entry is a question the door can ask with no model call: `text` is what the member reads, `choices` what they can tap. Every choice is a phrase the door reads back as that choice, so tapping it (or typing it) settles the question; `tests/test_clarify_registry.py` holds each one to that. WHEN a question is open is code, not data (`definition_conversation.open_questions`), read from what the planner already found. The ORDER here is the order asked: one question per turn, the first that is open. A choice that is a convention the product already holds (RSI 14 of the close, MACD 12/26/9, a library entry's own numbers) is never a question here. `also` lists the plain words a member may TYPE for a choice ("simple", "exponential"); an answer holding one is read as that choice. `remember` says what an ANSWER does next time (api/services/indicator_memory.py, the member's own account): `default` = the door uses the member's last answer instead of asking and says so (`as_before`); `offer` = the question is still asked, with their last answer first. `values` names each choice's closed value; nothing a member typed is ever stored. `title` is what the question is called in Settings ("What Create Indicator remembers"). A question with an `acronym` is asked when a request uses those letters and names neither indicator they could mean: `rows` maps each choice to the name-catalogue row it stands for (the likeliest first), and the answer follows that row's own path (a library entry builds checked; a withheld name is built with the name withheld; any other name gets the unknown-name answer). A question marked `number` takes any whole number of bars as its answer; its choices are the usual ones, and a choice may say more after the number ("252 (about 52 weeks)").

questions.open_when: the request says moving average (or MA, DMA) and names no kind of average
questions.as_before: Using {choice}, as you chose before. Name another kind to change it.
questions.title: Kind of moving average

questions.open_when: the request asks for an average and gives no number anywhere
questions.text: How many bars should the average use?
questions.title: Length of an average

questions.open_when: the request says price crosses something and does not say whether on the close or as soon as it trades through
choices: When the bar closes across it
As soon as price trades through it
questions.as_before: A cross counts {choice}, as you chose before. Say otherwise to change it.

said.When the bar closes across it: when the bar closes across it
said.As soon as price trades through it: as soon as price trades through it

questions.title: When a cross counts
